stories.title: Nobel laureate Machado: ‘Illegitimate’ Venezuela regime has no right to strike US oil deal
bullet_points: Opposition leader says interim government lacking democratic mandate to negotiate on natural resources   • The US and Venezuela: a century-old relationship drenched in oil   The Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has questioned Donald Trump’s oil deal with Venezuela’s interim government, saying the country’s natural resources do not belong to “an illegitimate regime”.

In her first public comments since  Trump announced  what he called “the biggest oil deal in world history” with Venezuela last Friday, Machado walked a diplomatic tightrope between challenging the agreement and trying not to rile the White House.

The address on Thursday followed the emergence of a police report, commissioned by a judge and widely quoted in the media, claiming Moroccan border forces had actively aided about 70,000 people to cross the border in late July.

stories.title: ‘We continue to suffer’: victims of apartheid-era Sharpeville massacre demand compensation
bullet_points: Claim relating to 1960 attack on hundreds of protesters part of wave of litigation over apartheid crimes in South Africa  The day dawned brightly on 21 March 1960, as residents of the South African township of Sharpeville gathered to protest against pass laws, which forced “Black, Indian and Coloured” South Africans to carry documents at all times specifying where they were allowed to be.
Abraham Mofokeng joined the march, one of dozens organised nationwide by the Pan Africanist Congress (PAC), a breakaway group from the African National Congress (ANC).
You could not have suspected that the day would go so horribly,” said Mofokeng, who was then a 20-year-old factory worker.

stories.title: The US and Venezuela: a century-old relationship drenched in oil

“All US policies toward Venezuela are affected in greater or less degree by the objective of assuring an adequate supply of petroleum for the US,”  the 1950 document  reads.
